close_reason:
Fixed in 20a10c1. MemoryBackend.update_object now enforces RFC 9610 §2 at-most-one-default invariant for AddressBook: when the patched object becomes default, all other previously-default AddressBooks in the same account are demoted in the same critical section. Demoted ids are recorded in the change_log so AddressBook/changes surfaces them per RFC 8620 §5.2.

Kept Ok(None) return — that is workspace canonical per crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/mod.rs:1223 ('MemoryBackend does not echo server-modified fields'). The bead's framing on Ok(None) was imprecise: per RFC 8620 §5.3, Ok(Some) is for server-set fields ON THE PATCHED OBJECT, not for side-effect changes to OTHER objects. The handler-side concern about demoted books appearing in the wire 'updated' map for the regular update path (today only the onSuccessSetIsDefault block re-fetches other books) is tracked at bd:JMAP-qz9v.5.

Three new integration tests on MemoryBackend exercise: promote-via-update demotes other books, demoted ids surface in /changes updated, idempotent re-promote of already-default book. 94+31+1 tests pass; workspace clippy + tests green.
description:
Trigger: any AddressBook/set update or ContactCard/set update against MemoryBackend.

Bad behavior: memory.rs:646-702 applies the merge-patch to the stored value, bumps state, records the change-log entry, and then returns Ok(None) unconditionally (line 701). Per RFC 8620 §5.3, returning None means 'the patch was applied verbatim and the client already has the updated state; emit the id with a null value in the updated map'. Returning Some(obj) means 'the server set additional fields beyond what the client requested; emit the full obj in updated so the client picks them up'.

For MemoryBackend this is mostly fine — the merge-patch IS the verbatim story. But the handler-level onSuccessSetIsDefault flow at addressbook.rs:354-372 RELIES on update_object returning Some(obj) to populate the updated map with the demoted books — and even more specifically, the addressbook.rs handler ALWAYS reaches the post-update fallback re-fetch loop (lines 354-372) because update_object never returns Some.

So the MemoryBackend implicitly forces the handler to re-fetch every other AddressBook from scratch on every isDefault transition. That's an O(N) scan per transition where it could have been O(1) (the backend already cleared the flag on a single book; just return Some(promoted) and let the handler trust the caller).

For Contacts this is a perf concern, not a correctness one. But the deeper issue is that MemoryBackend.update_object ALSO does not maintain the single-default invariant during a regular update where isDefault: true is set. Compare MockBackend.update_object at lib.rs:427-435 which DOES enforce single-default — the reference impl is LESS realistic than the test mock. Contributors studying memory.rs to learn the pattern will copy a backend that doesn't enforce the invariant. See JMAP-qz9v.5 for the broader single-default-on-create bug.
title: MemoryBackend.update_object always returns Ok(None) even after applying a patch — handler emits 'updated: { id: null }' instead of server-set echo
